rust.name: src/books.rs:258:70: replace > with >= in window_status
rust.why: A limit without its own reset can expose the reading’s reset at the exact second it expires, while the tests cover a future fallback reset.

rust.name: src/books.rs:337:39: replace / with % in at_reset
rust.why: This removes the minimum elapsed time for the tested window lengths, and the single-reading pace tests leave enough elapsed time that the floor never decides the outcome.

rust.name: src/time.rs:73:29: replace || with && in parse
rust.why: A six-byte offset such as +09X00 would pass, while the malformed offset in the tests has both the wrong length and the wrong separator.

rust.name: src/time.rs:81:33: replace % with / in parse
rust.why: This would accept February 29 in 2100, and the existing 2100 case stops at February 28.

rust.name: src/time.rs:42:37: replace || with && in parse
rust.why: A date with just one wrong hyphen separator could parse because the numeric fields are sliced separately and the tests omit that malformed shape.
